title: UPS 2976: 29 Feet — What the NTSB Has Found So Far (MD-11, Louisville)
description:
November 4, 2025: UPS flight 2976, a McDonnell Douglas MD-11F, lifts off from Louisville and never climbs higher than 29 feet. Three crew members and eleven people on the ground were killed. This video walks through what the NTSB has published so far: the preliminary report, the January 2026 investigative update, the public docket of the May 2026 investigative hearing, the NTSB's own animation, and the board's media briefings.

The investigation (NTSB DCA26MA024) is NOT finished. The NTSB has not determined a probable cause, and neither do we. Everything here is attributed to the NTSB as "so far", and every document or image from a party to the investigation is labelled as theirs. We do not say what caused the accident.

firstComment: The NTSB says it hopes to have answers no later than May 2027. Until then, four questions are still open: why the airplane did not climb, how the bearing race and lugs came to be in that condition, what reached operators over the years, and what the FAA's design rules require when a pylon fails. Which one do you most want the board to answer?
